raw_response:
I'll think this through as the farmer and then give my plan.

My 15 mu sits on the North China Plain — good flat ground, well water is reliable but the groundwater table keeps dropping, so I cannot waste water like 20 years ago. With only two of us at home and some off-farm work, I need a plan that doesn't eat all my labor at once.

Here is how I split the land this year:
- 10 mu on wheat-maize double crop (my main rotation)
- 5 mu on cotton — cotton price has been so-so, but it spreads my risk and the land I put cotton on is sandier, not the best for wheat

**Winter wheat (10 mu)** — I already planted last October. Variety Jimai 22, improved. Base fertilizer I applied 40 kg diammonium phosphate + 15 kg urea + 10 kg potassium sulfate per mu before sowing. Top-dressing at green-up/jointing I'll put another 15 kg urea. Total about 16 kg N, 7 kg P, 5 kg K per mu. Irrigate 3 times — over-winter water already done, then jointing, then grain-filling. Spray twice: one for aphids and powdery mildew at booting, one "yi pen san fang" at flowering for scab, aphids, and mites together. I expect 520 kg/mu — last two years I hit 500-540.

**Summer maize (10 mu)** — after wheat harvest in mid-June, I direct-seed Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid, no-till, with the seeder right behind the combine. Base 30 kg compound (15-15-15) per mu at sowing, then 20 kg urea side-dressed at big-trumpet stage. Total N ~15 kg, P 4.5 kg, K 4.5 kg per mu. Irrigate twice if rain is short — usually jointing and tasseling. One pesticide spray for corn borer and armyworm at whorl stage, sometimes a second if fall armyworm shows up. Expect 600 kg/mu.

**Cotton (5 mu)** — ploughed in spring, I'll transplant Bt hybrid seedlings in late April. Base 25 kg compound + 10 kg urea per mu, then top-dress 15 kg urea at flowering-boll stage. About 14 kg N, 5 kg P, 8 kg K per mu — cotton wants more potassium for boll quality. Irrigate 3 times. Pesticide 4 times — even with Bt, I still get aphids, spider mites, and late-season bollworm pressure. Expect 260 kg seed cotton/mu.

I keep fertilizer a little on the generous side — losing 50 kg of wheat costs me more than an extra bag of urea. But I've cut back from what I used 10 years ago because I've seen that piling on nitrogen past a point just makes the wheat fall over.
